_note: SERP snapshot built from the competing-coverage section of the CBAM research dossier. Every URL was fetched directly with curl.exe (2026-10-03, HTTP 200) and again while verifying that the gate can load each competitor page; page contents were read from the downloaded copies, never from search snippets. Provenance: search discovery, then direct fetch verification. taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu, dehst.de, emissieautoriteit.nl and fu.gov.si are official publishers and are excluded from the competitor set automatically, so they are not listed here. Only the first three results enter the TOP_N comparison, and all three are steel-only: none carries a table of per-tonne costs with a currency amount, and none covers aluminium.

results.title: [SMM Analysis] Carbon Comes Due: A Full Breakdown of the New CBAM Rules & the Country-Cost Inversion for Flagship Steels
results.snippet: Chinese HRC bears about 163 EUR/tonne, 26% of value. Billet, HRC and CRC within one origin are nearly identical (China 162 / 163 / 158 EUR/tonne). The CBAM factor - the share of free allocation not yet phased out - falls from 97.5% in 2026 to 0% by 2034.

results.title: [SMM Analysis] SMM launches stainless steel CBAM calculator: Indonesian 304 CRC carries a EUR626/mt CBAM bill into the EU
results.snippet: SMM launches a stainless steel CBAM calculator. Indonesian 304 cold-rolled coil carries a EUR626 per tonne CBAM bill into the EU under the 2026 country default values.

results.title: Italian rerollers and buyers call CBAM values unworkable, actual emissions verification a priority in 2026
results.snippet: Per-origin 2026 default-value cost estimates attributed to Fastmarkets for steel slab only: China approximately EUR 144/t, Russia EUR 149/t, India EUR 230/t, Indonesia EUR 541/t, Brazil EUR 22/t.
